subject: ant queen
title: A Parasite Queen Makes Ants Kill Their Own Mother

scenes.text: This ant queen takes over a colony without killing anyone herself.
She sneaks into a nest of yellow meadow ants and finds their queen.
Then she sprays her with a chemical, about fifteen times over twenty hours.
The spray makes the queen smell like an enemy to her own colony.
So her daughters turn on her and tear her apart. Within about four days, she's dead.
And the same workers raise the invader's babies instead. She never lifted a jaw.

description:
A parasitic ant queen, Lasius orientalis, invades colonies of other Lasius ants. She repeatedly sprays the resident queen with a chemical (thought to be formic acid), about 15 times over 20 hours.
The resident queen's own workers then attack and kill her, and go on to raise the invader's brood. The study was published in Current Biology in November 2025.
Which is worse: the invader or the daughters?
first_comment: In a related species, just two sprays were enough. What should a colony do against a queen like this?
